statement: On the frozen R12 continuous-fit study with constant learning rate .05, increasing whole-run random_strength from 0 to 10 increased the normalized maximum train slope-scan score in both environments: synthetic mean paired difference 0.017136016867994843 (adjusted family4 95% CI [0.00759461814522553,0.026677415590764156]) and breast_cancer 0.003238597748487245 (CI [0.0014128320519830092,0.005064363444991481]). All six prespecified fixed late-event gates at tree 512 with 64-point windows returned not_established under the family12 gain/drop intervals, practical after-drop >.01, and at least 10/12 positive-gain rule. Descriptively, 63/72 models reached exact zero train classification errors at first-zero iterations 123-988, while training LogLoss at first zero reached 0.14022221881182134. Whole-run parameter effects do not identify split-noise annealing, a natural late-acceleration mechanism, or double descent; failure of this fixed-window gate does not exclude events elsewhere.
limitations: Whole-run random_strength interventions change tree partitions, gradient history and entire loss range. A positive normalized maximum-scan contrast does not isolate the internal annealing law, a localized late event or a causal mechanism of natural acceleration.

The primary max scan can concern early dynamics. All six fixed late-window gatesnot_established apply only to boundary512 and64-point windows with practical drop.01 and>=10/12 positive gains. This is not evidence that acceleration is absent everywhere.
